evidence: The original tuple held three reads under a comment saying "four" while README documents five non-health GETs; ff3a8ea adds `/v1/voices/{voice_id}` and `/v1/voices/{voice_id}/settings` as templates, which closes the gap AUTH-2's "every documented endpoint" claim is about.
guidance_note: When a probe claims to cover 'every documented endpoint', derive or test-pin the probed set against the documented table (README) in the original PR, for every method, rather than hand-listing a subset.

evidence: Duplicate of F1 on the same comment/tuple; the same ff3a8ea change fixes both and the count was dropped from the comment.

Both `Broken` branches of `probe_auth_2` were reachable only by a partly-guarded server no test built; ff3a8ea adds `partly_guarded_deployment` and parametrized tests, and the agent mutation-checked each branch independently (== 401 to == 499).
guidance_note: For every Broken branch a probe adds, add the adversarial fixture that reaches it in the same commit, across all probes in the file, not only the one under discussion.

evidence: After ff3a8ea widened the GET set, `probe_auth_2` still made one synthesis via `_spoken` to the plain route while README documents four POST routes; the agent itself calls it "the same gap one side over" and f7fe9c7 adds `DOCUMENTED_SYNTHESES` plus a README-equality test.
guidance_note: When widening a probed set to match the documented surface, sweep every method in that surface (GET and POST) in the same fix, and pin it with an equality test against the document.

evidence: Duplicate of F4 (three undocumented-for POST variants unprobed); reply-hint is unclear but the thread plans and lands the same f7fe9c7 fix.

`probe_health_1` called `_health_voices`, which raised `Blocked` on a body with no `voices` array, so HEALTH-1's own subject reported unasked; the flag is a false positive because f7fe9c7 touched only AUTH-2, README and its tests, and this logic predates review.
guidance_note: When a claim's subject is a response's shape, parse that shape inside the claim (returning the complaint) rather than through a shared precondition helper that raises Blocked, as DISC-1 already did.

evidence: `_health_voices` checked only that `voices` was a list, so `{"voices": [{"id": "v1"}]}` reached `name not in listed` and raised TypeError out of the run; the agent reproduced the crash, and 01b342c stamps each entry as a non-empty string. The code predates review, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: When parsing untrusted JSON, stamp element types for every collection that later goes into a set or dict lookup, matching the existing per-entry parser (`_parsed_voices`).

evidence: The new paragraph said a key was not necessary for HEALTH-3 while the table row still read "(only when the prober holds a key)"; 01b342c rewrites the row to "(only against a guarded deployment)" and also corrects the paragraph's false "sufficient". The paragraph came from the original PR (f7fe9c7 did not touch docs), so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: When writing prose that corrects a table's qualifier, edit the table cell in the same change, especially when the equality test strips that parenthetical.

evidence: F3's fix added adversarial tests for AUTH-2's Broken branches only; HEALTH-1's off-contract status, HEALTH-3's 401 and AUTH-1's not-closed branches stayed untested, and the agent calls it "the same finding as last round's". 01b342c adds fixtures for all of them through a generalised `guarded_deployment`.
guidance_note: When a reviewer flags one probe's untested Broken branches, enumerate every Broken return in the module and cover them all in that same fix.

evidence: Duplicate of F8 on the same doc line, fixed by the same 01b342c table-row edit; it comes from the original PR, not from f7fe9c7.

Both loops in `probe_auth_2` judged only `== 401`, so a 403 or 500 fell through to Held; 01b342c merges them into one loop over `_keyless_asks` where anything but 2xx or 404 is Broken. The `== 401` check predates review, and the status axis is a separate gap from the endpoint-set gap F1/F4 fixed, so it is not attributed to them.
guidance_note: When a probe decides 'answered vs refused', define it as the positive case (2xx, plus documented exemptions) rather than matching one refusal status this checkout happens to use.

evidence: 01b342c dropped the 401-only assumption in `probe_auth_2` but left `guarded = keyless.status == 401` in `discover()`, which every claim branches on. The agent took the reviewer's allow-list arm (`AUTH_REFUSALS = (401, 403)`) and gave a defensible reason for not treating every non-2xx as guarded (a 500 is a listing defect).
guidance_note: When removing a hard-coded status assumption from one check, grep the module for every comparison against that status and fix them together, starting with the entrypoint other claims depend on.

evidence: `--timeout` was `type=float` and passed straight into `Target`, so a negative value raised ValueError past `_ask`'s except; the agent reproduced exit 1 (the 'claims broken' code). The argparse setup is original PR code, unchanged by 01b342c, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: Validate every numeric CLI argument with an argparse `type=` that rejects out-of-range values, so bad input can never reach the code that maps exceptions to exit codes.

evidence: ff3a8ea (F1's fix) rewrote the `DOCUMENTED_READS` comment to "every gettable path README publishes", while the tuple and the later equality test deliberately exclude `/health`; the agent concedes "The comment is mine from two rounds ago".
guidance_note: When rewriting a comment that states a set's membership, check it against the exclusions the code and its test actually encode (`published["GET"] - {"/health"}`).

narrative: The PR's main defect was a probed surface narrower than the documented one, and it was fixed one axis per round: GET reads (F1), then POST syntheses (F4/F5), then refusal statuses (F11), then the guard-detection entrypoint (F12). The same pattern hit tests: F3's fix covered AUTH-2's branches only, and F9 found the rest. Round 1 was entirely caused by F1's incomplete sweep. Rounds 2 and 3 also carried independent pre-existing findings (F6, F7, F13), so they would have happened anyway. The agent's fixes were sound and mutation-verified, and it built a README-equality test so the endpoint axis is pinned.
guidance_observations: The agent noticed the 'same defect, next axis' pattern only after three rounds; naming the defect class at the first finding and sweeping every axis then (methods, statuses, entrypoint) would have collapsed F4, F5, F11 and F12 into round 0's fix.
Duplicate findings (F1/F2, F4/F5, F8/F10) were correctly answered with one fix posted on both threads.
Round 5 hit the MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS cap, so head commit 7fada6e merged unreviewed.

evidence: The crash is real: `_supported_arrays` recurses in Python with no bound and RecursionError is not caught by `_finding`. The agent says, from its own run, that the attribution to `json.loads` was wrong. The 4f3edff fix puts the walk inside the same try and returns a Broken for RecursionError, which is one of the reviewer's two offered arms and holds whichever half raises.
guidance_note: When a probe recursively walks untrusted JSON, put the walk inside the same try that guards the parse and map RecursionError to a verdict in the original PR.

evidence: `_keyless_asks` built `f"{path}?output_format={PCM_FORMAT}"` by hand beside `_posted`'s own suffix, contradicting the 'one place' docstring. The agent extracted only the duplicated piece, `_in_format`, keeping `_keyless_asks` pure rather than routing it through effectful `_posted`, and deleted the false single-enforcer sentence; 4f3edff shows both call sites using it.
guidance_note: Before writing a '[LAW:single-enforcer] the one place' docstring, grep for the string the function builds (`?output_format=`) to confirm no other site builds it.

evidence: One branch covering not-a-string, blank and too-long text was labelled `string_too_short`; 4f3edff changes it to the reviewer's suggested `value_error`, which the prober never reads.

`set(arrays[0])` over objects raises TypeError, which `_finding` does not catch. 4f3edff adds `_is_name_array` so `_supported_arrays` returns `list[list[str]]` and an array of objects falls into the existing 'carries no supported array' Broken. That is the reviewer's 'treat as broken' remedy moved into the parser, with a test confirmed to bite.
guidance_note: When a parser stamps a container type for untrusted JSON, stamp its element type too whenever a later line hashes the elements.

evidence: `_refused` and `probe_refusal` each call `_asked`, so the 'one request, two readings' docstring was false. The agent took the reviewer's second arm (fix the docstring) and gave a sound reason not to cache: a 422 refusal is a cheap idempotent POST, unlike the 30-synthesis `Spoken` draw.
guidance_note: Don't justify a function by analogy to a sibling ('for the reason _parsed_voices has two') without checking the sibling's actual mechanism matches.

evidence: Duplicate of F4 (the same `set(arrays[0])` TypeError); the same `_is_name_array` change in 4f3edff closes it, and the reply was posted on both threads.

`name.encode() not in answer.body` let `context` satisfy `text` and, as the agent found, `unsupported` satisfy `supported`. 4f3edff matches on `\b` word boundaries; the test is confirmed to bite and a live run against piper stayed at 19 held / 2 unasked.
guidance_note: When implementing a rule stated as 'the body names X', write a negative test where X appears only inside a longer word, before shipping a substring check.

evidence: Seven mp3 plus five opus names carry a bitrate, twelve not five; the agent counted them programmatically and 4f3edff fixes the word.
guidance_note: Compute counts stated in comments from the table they describe instead of writing them by eye.

evidence: The regression test added in 4f3edff for F7 falls back to `_refused(output_format, body)`, which returns None for every non-refused request, so the fixture served 200 `null` for all format draws; the agent concedes "a real bug in a test I added last round". 4c0a5b0 switches to `conformant` and adds FMT-2/FMT-3 held assertions that bite.
guidance_note: When adding a fixture variant, copy the fallback every sibling fixture uses (`conformant(...)`) and assert at least one unrelated claim still holds, so a broken stand-in cannot pass silently.

evidence: F7's fix (4f3edff) replaced the substring check with `_names`' word-boundary match but left docs/conformance-claims.md saying the rule is "checked as raw-byte substrings"; 4c0a5b0 rewrites the sentence to say word-bounded, with the reason.
guidance_note: When a fix changes how a documented rule is enforced, grep the authority doc for the old mechanism's wording ("substring") and update it in the same commit.

evidence: The module docstring's "five claims" disagreed with `Spoken`'s "eight"; the agent removed the duplicate count rather than syncing it. The flag is a false positive: the line was added by the original PR, and 4f3edff never touched it.
guidance_note: Don't restate a count in an overview that a closer docstring already owns; point at the owner.

evidence: The comment above `CLAIMS` still said e16.4 claims were 'remaining' while this PR adds FMT-1..8 and REF-1..7 below it. The line is unchanged pre-review text, so the ON-NAMED-FIX flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: When landing a ticket's rows into a registry, update any adjacent 'remaining tickets' comment in the same commit.

evidence: Duplicate of F10 on the same doc line, closed by the same 4c0a5b0 rewrite; the drift is from F7's 4f3edff change to `_names`.

narrative: Round 0 found real robustness and comment bugs, and the agent answered each with a seam-level fix plus mutation-checked tests. F7's fix caused three round-1 findings: a broken fallback in its own regression test (F9), and the authority doc still describing the rejected substring rule (F10/F13). Round 1 also had two pre-existing stale comments (F11, F12) the reviewer missed in round 0, so it would have happened anyway. Round 2 approved.
guidance_observations: The fix for F7 changed an enforced rule without grepping the documentation that calls itself the authority for that rule, producing a duplicate pair of drift findings.
New regression fixtures twice nearly proved nothing (the json.dumps 500 in F1, the null fallback in F9); asserting an unrelated claim still holds under each new fixture would catch both.

evidence: `.spoke()` turns a composed-and-refused draw into Blocked, so a voice declaring timestamps whose endpoints refuse reads unasked. The agent added `Asked.refusal(draw)`, wired into CAP-1/2/3 and MOD-3/6 with a test per claim that fails with the wiring removed; this is the reviewer's explicit status check, done once at the seam.
guidance_note: When a claim requires a served draw, distinguish 'could not compose' from 'deployment refused' at the reader seam in the original design, rather than routing both through one Blocked path.

evidence: `probe_disc_5` read only `language`/`id` but went through the all-or-nothing `Catalogue`; 110aaa0 reads `deployment.voices` and blocks only on the language itself, naming DISC-1 as owner, with tests in both directions.
guidance_note: Route each claim through the narrowest parsed view that carries the fields it reads, so an unrelated field's parse failure cannot gate it.

evidence: The agent agreed the gate was real but deferred it to ticket e16.d0b scoped to six `.once` claims. F10 then shows `_ask_each_voice` calls `_declarations(listing)` before building anything, so roughly 22 claims are gated, not six. The deferral rested on an undercounted blast radius and filed a ticket too narrow to fix it.
guidance_note: Before deferring a finding to a ticket, trace the failing call (`_declarations`) to every caller it gates and put that full list in the ticket, rather than adopting the reviewer's enumerated subset.

evidence: `probe_disc_2` compares only `voice_id`, so attributing the both-bodies alias rewrite to DISC-2 was false; the agent confirmed this and 110aaa0 replaced the sentence with the real reason.
guidance_note: When a fixture docstring names a claim as the reason, check that claim's probe actually reads that field.

evidence: `probe_disc_2` used `deployment.asking().catalogue.voices` while needing only ids; 110aaa0 switches to `deployment.voices`, with a test where one voice's malformed `capabilities` leaves DISC-2/DISC-5 askable, confirmed to fail when the fix is reverted.

The hunk shows `spoken.add(spoke)` after a guard that short-circuits on None, so None entered the set and Held overcounted voices it never checked; 110aaa0 `continue`s on a missing header, which is equivalent to the suggested guard.
guidance_note: When a loop guard skips a None, make the accumulation line skip it too.

evidence: `_ask_each_voice` raises Blocked on an empty listing before `Asking` exists, so the six raw callers' empty-subject messages were unreachable. The agent replaced them with one `NO_VOICE_OFFERED` constant plus a comment saying why it is unreachable, and kept the filtered callers' reachable messages.

F1's fix added `refusal()` for non-200 answers, but a 200 with an empty body still goes through `_served`, which the reviewer says raises Blocked. That is the remaining case of the same 'deployment lie masked as unasked' class, but `_served`'s body is not in the packet. The thread has no reply because the PR merged at 13:59 while this review (posted 14:13) was still running.
guidance_note: When splitting 'refused' from 'not composed' at a seam, enumerate every way a served answer can fail the claim (non-200, empty 200) and route all of them to the deployment's verdict.

evidence: The hunk shows `tuple(part.strip() for part in named.split(","))`, which maps an empty header to `("",)`, a truthy value that defeats the `or 'absent'` evidence strings. The flag is a false positive: 56a1d7c only added a CAP-5 docstring, and `_ignored` is original PR code. The PR merged with the thread unanswered.
guidance_note: When parsing a comma-separated header, drop empty parts so an empty header and an absent one parse to distinguishable, honest values.

evidence: The hunk confirms `_ask_each_voice` starts with `voices = _declarations(listing)`, so one voice's malformed `aliases` gates every `asking()` caller, not the six the e16.d0b ticket names. F3's deferral undercounted the scope. The claim that the catalogue needs only language/models is not verifiable from the packet. Unanswered; the PR merged before this round posted.
guidance_note: When filing a deferral ticket, list the gated callers by tracing the raising function's call graph, not by copying the reviewer's enumeration.

evidence: ø, î and ñ are all latin-1 code points, so describing `UNPRINTABLE_VOICE` as 'bytes are not latin-1' is false, and the PR's SUB-2 doc says the rule is printable ASCII. The flag is a false positive: 56a1d7c touched only a CAP-5 docstring, and the packet does not show the SUB-2 correction landing in a review fix. Unanswered at merge.
guidance_note: When a doc corrects a criterion (latin-1 to printable ASCII), grep the code for every comment and message stating the old criterion and fix them in the same change.

narrative: Round 0's seven findings were real and six were fixed well at their seams, with tests confirmed to bite. F3 was deferred to a ticket scoped to six claims, and round 1's F10 shows the same gate covers about 22. F8 is the leftover case of F1's refused-vs-unasked split. Round 1 would have happened regardless because F9 and F11 are pre-existing, but none of its four findings got a reply: the PR merged at 13:59, while round 1 (started 13:52) was still running, and it posted CHANGES_REQUESTED at 14:13.
guidance_observations: The agent merged while a review round on its head commit was in flight, leaving four findings, including a widened-scope correction to its own deferral ticket, unanswered on a merged PR.
The deferral in F3 was argued carefully but rested on a blast radius copied from the reviewer instead of traced from the raising call, so the ticket under-scopes the fix.
